description:
Pune Startup Fest, started in 2019, is COEP Technological University’s annual entrepreneurship initiative organized by COEP Tech's E-Cell. Over the years, Pune Startup Fest has grown into a prominent platform for startups, investors, mentors, and students.
At its core, Pune Startup Fest ’26 aims to bring together startups, students, investors, mentors, industry leaders, C-level executives, and the wider public from across the country, creating a collaborative ecosystem that fuels innovation and accelerates entrepreneurial growth.
PSF ’26 is more than a festival, it is a platform where ideas evolve into impact, and pioneers ascend.

competitions.name: INNOVATOR'S RELAY
competitions.description: A multi-stage innovation challenge designed to test originality, adaptability, teamwork, and strategic thinking.
competitions.commonRulesMessage:
Eligibility: Open to all college students.
Individual Participation: Round 1 begins with solo participants.
Teams are formed only in later rounds through random selection.

1.	All team assignments are random and final.
2.	Time limits are strictly enforced.
3.	All submitted ideas must be original.
4.	Professional and respectful conduct is mandatory.
5.	Judges' decisions are final.
6.	Failure to participate in assigned teams may result in disqualification.
7.	Plagiarism or misconduct results in immediate disqualification.
8.	The number of advancing teams may vary based on participation.
9.	The organizing committee holds the right to modify rules if required.
10.	Final decisions regarding disputes or violations rest with the organizers.
rounds:
@{roundNumber=1; title=Solo Innovation; description=; rules=System.Object[]; roundRulesMessage=Round 1 is based on 18 curated problem statements related to real college ecosystem challenges. Teams will receive their prompt through a random chit-selection, ensuring fairness and encouraging creativity and adaptability.
Objective: Create an original and innovative product.
Participants get 10 minutes to ideate and 60 seconds to pitch, covering the problem, solution, target users, and key features (sketch optional).
Ideas will be judged on creativity, practical viability, and wow factor (1–10 each).
The top 50% of participants will qualify for Round 2.; dateTime=; venue=COEP Technological University; _id=696f37926f11efa023d02477}

@{roundNumber=2; title=Team Fusion (Teams of Two); description=; rules=System.Object[]; roundRulesMessage=Advancing participants are paired through random chit selection. Each team must merge their Round 1 ideas into a single hybrid innovation.
Teams get 10–15 minutes to collaborate and develop the concept, followed by a 2-minute pitch. The final output should include an integrated product idea, a unified brand name, and a clear market purpose.
The pitch must explain how the ideas were merged, why the combined product is stronger, and its unique value proposition. Evaluation is based on integration quality, innovation, market potential, and team collaboration.
The top 50% of teams advance to Round 3.; dateTime=; venue=COEP Technological University; _id=696f37926f11efa023d02478}

@{roundNumber=3; title=Expansion Innovation (Teams of Four); description=; rules=System.Object[]; roundRulesMessage=Advancing participants are regrouped through random selection, forming teams of four by merging two winning pairs. This ensures fresh collaboration dynamics.
Objective: Build a comprehensive, multi-component product ecosystem.
Teams get 20 minutes for discussion and integration, followed by a 5-minute final pitch. The solution should present a connected ecosystem (such as product + app or service + platform), supported by use cases, a clear brand story, and market impact.
The pitch must explain ecosystem integration, key differentiators, scalability, and potential impact. Teams are evaluated on cohesion, creativity, business feasibility, and presentation quality.
Outcome: One team is crowned the overall winner.; dateTime=; venue=COEP Technological University; _id=696f37926f11efa023d02479}

competitions.name: BIDWARS
competitions.description: Put your analytical skills to the test and bid for players to create your cricket team.
competitions.commonRulesMessage:
General Rules
1. Event is open to all participants
2. Team size must be exactly 2 members
3. Each team will be given a virtual budget of ₹50 Crore
4. Each team can buy a maximum of 5 players
5. Team composition must include:
   a. At least one batsman
   b. At least one bowler
   c. At least one wicket-keeper
   d. At least one all-rounder
6. Buying a 3rd player of the same type may lead to disqualification
7. A maximum of 2 overseas players is allowed per team
8. Bidding for a 3rd overseas player will lead to disqualification

Player Tiers & Base Prices
1. Players are divided into four tiers:
2. Tier 1: 85–100 points | Base Price: ₹5 Crore
3. Tier 2: 70–84 points | Base Price: ₹3 Crore
4. Tier 3: 55–69 points | Base Price: ₹1 Crore
5. Tier 4: 25–54 points | Base Price: ₹20 Lakhs
6. Player value points will be disclosed 15 minutes before the auction
7. Player valuations are final and decided by auction managers

Elimination & Tie-Breaker Rules
1. Top 2 teams from each group qualify for Round 2
2. Top 3 teams in Round 2 are declared winners
3. Tie-breaker priority:
4. Higher remaining budget
5. Fewer overseas players
6. Teams exceeding budget will be disqualified immediately
7. Teams violating player type or overseas limits may be reviewed and disqualified

competitions.commonRulesMessage:

rounds:
@{roundNumber=1; title=Startup Investment Simulation; description=Fund Arcade consists of two rounds:; rules=System.Object[]; roundRulesMessage=Description
1. Teams receive 8 startup canvases displayed for 2 minutes each
2. Each team gets ₹100 Cr virtual currency to invest
3. Minimum investment is ₹5 Cr and maximum is ₹45 Cr per startup
4. Teams must invest in at least 3 startups
5. Startup outcomes are hidden and revealed after portfolio lock
6. Returns are calculated using predefined multipliers
7. Performance is scored based on total ROI

Rules
1. Investment limits and diversification are mandatory
2. Portfolios cannot be changed after submission
3. Any malpractice will lead to disqualification; dateTime=; venue=COEP Technological University; _id=696f37d26f11efa023d02520}

@{roundNumber=2; title=Exit Strategy Simulation; description=; rules=System.Object[]; roundRulesMessage=Description
1. Teams qualify based on Round 1 ROI
2. Each team receives a Base Score (highest ROI = 100)
3. Teams choose one exit strategy with fixed multiplier and risk
4. Risk outcome is decided publicly
5. Final Score = Base Score × Multiplier × Risk
6. Highest Final Score wins the event

Rules
1. Exit strategy choice is final
2. Risk outcome must be accepted
3. Organisers’ decisions are final; dateTime=; venue=COEP Technological University; _id=696f37d26f11efa023d02521}

competitions.name: SURVIVE & THRIVE
competitions.description: A startup crisis simulation challenge where participants act as founders making tough decisions under pressure.
competitions.commonRulesMessage:
1. Evaluation is 30% subjective and 70% objective
2. Subjective evaluation includes adaptability, reasoning, analysis, and clarity
3. Objective scoring is based on survival score formula
4. Survival Score = (Funds – Cost – Churn Loss) × Reputation Multiplier
5. Objective Marks = (Survival Score ÷ Max Score) × 70
6. Each round tests finance, customer trust, and operations
7. Misconduct or unfair practices lead to disqualification
8. Organizers’ decisions are final and binding
rounds:
@{roundNumber=1; title=Crisis Announcement; description=; rules=System.Object[]; roundRulesMessage=1. Each round begins with a startup crisis scenario
2. Teams receive 4 strategic options (A–D)
3. Each option includes details of funds gained, costs incurred, churn percentage, and reputation score
4. Teams must analyze the options and select one within the given time; dateTime=; venue=COEP Technological University; _id=695a92be7035e620403c8b39}

@{roundNumber=2; title=The Twist; description=; rules=System.Object[]; roundRulesMessage=1. A mid-round twist is announced affecting the chosen options
2. The twist modifies either churn percentage or reputation score
3. Teams are given 2 minutes to adapt their strategy
4. Teams must justify how they respond to the twist; dateTime=; venue=COEP Technological University; _id=695a92be7035e620403c8b3a}

@{roundNumber=3; title=Team Presentation; description=; rules=System.Object[]; roundRulesMessage=1. Each team presents their final strategy
2. Teams explain calculations using the given formula
3. Teams describe how they handled the twist
4. Teams justify their final decision-making
5. Presentation time is limited to 3 minutes per team; dateTime=; venue=COEP Technological University; _id=695a92be7035e620403c8b3b}

competitions.name: COURTROOM CLASH
competitions.description: A dynamic, two-round IPR advocacy event designed to assess participants’ legal reasoning, argumentation skills, commercial awareness, and strategic adaptability.
competitions.commonRulesMessage:
1. Event is open to all participants
2. Team size must be exactly 2 members
3. Participants must adhere strictly to allotted time limits
4. Arguments and presentations must remain relevant to the proposition
5. Any form of misconduct or unprofessional behavior may lead to disqualification
6. The organizing committee reserves the right to modify rounds or guidelines if required
7. Judges’ and organizers’ decisions are final and binding
rounds:
@{roundNumber=1; title=Preliminary Round; description=; rules=System.Object[]; roundRulesMessage=Round Description
1. Ten teams will argue a structured IPR proposition
2. Teams will be assigned roles as either Appellant or Respondent
3. Teams will present oral arguments based on statutory interpretation and legal precedents
4. Arguments must be structured, reasoned, and professionally delivered
5. Top 4 teams will advance to the Final Round

Evaluation Criteria
1. Legal understanding and use of statutory provisions
2. Application of relevant precedents
3. Structure and clarity of arguments
4. Persuasiveness and legal reasoning
5. Courtroom etiquette and professionalism; dateTime=; venue=COEP Technological University; _id=696f37e46f11efa023d0255c}

@{roundNumber=2; title=Final Round; description=; rules=System.Object[]; roundRulesMessage=Round Description
1. The final round combines prepared strategy with spontaneous legal adaptability
2. Teams will address the same dispute from the Preliminary Round

Phase 1 – Strategic Resolution Pitch
1. Teams must propose a legally sound and commercially viable resolution
2. Solutions may include:
   1. Licensing or royalty frameworks
   2. Revenue-sharing or damages models
   3. Strategic modifications or design changes
   4. Business-focused settlements or coexistence strategies
3. This phase evaluates legal reasoning and business intelligence

Phase 2 – 30-Minute Twist Addendum
1. Teams receive a new factual or legal twist 30 minutes before presentation
2. The twist may involve:
   1. New prior art or registration
   2. Entry of a competing product
   3. Change in client business priorities
   4. New infringement or procedural issues
3. Teams must adapt their strategy accordingly; dateTime=; venue=COEP Technological University; _id=696f37e46f11efa023d0255d}
